steps.text: Mix ground beef, Worcestershire sauce, pepper, and garlic salt together in a bowl until well combined.
Form into eight thin patties, each slightly larger than a cheese slice.
Cut each slice of American cheese into 4 equal pieces; stack the pieces.
Sandwich one stack of cheese between 2 ground beef patties.
Tightly pinch the edges together to seal around the cheese. Be sure to seal tightly, or the cheese will burst through when cooked. Repeat with the remaining cheese and patties.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Cook patties in the hot skillet until well browned, about 4 minutes; they will puff up due to steam from the melting cheese.

Flip patties, prick the tops to release steam, and cook until browned on the other side and no longer pink in the center; about 4 more minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Juicy Lucy Burgers
raw_recipe.description: The famous Juicy Lucy burger, a favorite of Minnesotans, features melted American cheese sandwiched between two seasoned ground beef patties.

review.reviewBody: Minnesota's contribution to the culinary world! Don't forget to let this gem sit for a few minutes before taking your first bite, or you will have molten lava dribbling down your chin.

The recipe is very good as it is, but fantastic if you double the wochestershire sauce and I like to use 2 tsp of montreal steak seasoning in place of the garlic salt and pepper.
Two very important things - it is absolutely critical that you leave enough room on the edges to get a good seal. If the cheese runs out, not near as good. And by the way, if the cheese does start to run out, its done! Get it off the grill or pan before you lose your cheese! I tried to make this a little healthier with 94% lean burger....not near as good as when I made the exact same recipe with 80% lean. You need the fat and grease for a great burger.
BTW - I saw 1 review that gave 1 star because the cheese leaked out (user error) and 1 gave a low rating because the recipe has a lot of fat. REALLY? Rate on the quality of the recipe, not on your ability to cook or you opinion of what is healthy or not.

My husband and I loved this. 
I used only used a pound of 20% ground beef, added 2 Tbsps catsup, 1/3 cup finely chopped red onion, and outdoor grilled them. Never thought burgers would turn out that juicy and delicious. Great easy recipe.

Used the tips found in these reviews (added ~2t Montreal Steak seasoning in place of the garlic salt and pepper) and added more cheese (~1.5 Kraft slices, except I used Colby). Used fresh 93%/7% ground beef, and placed the prepared patties in the freezer for ~20 minutes prior to griddling, then rested for ~4 minutes prior to eating. Held together beautifully and wonderfully juicy!

Again, Chef John never disappoints! it poured down rain I couldn’t grill my burgers I put them in a frying pan on an electric range. Yum! Super, juicy, tasty! Best Indoor Burger. Next time I’m going to put Blue Cheese in the middle! as long as you put the two burgers together and refrigerate them for an hour or two they hold together really well.
Made patties litter thicker and added more Worcestershire sauce. Cooked on the grill and they were a big hit!

I don’t like using salt of any kind, so use garlic powder + pepper instead. I read a cooking tip for burgers that I have yet to try… freeze a stick of butter, grate some into the burger mix, like cheese, then mix & form patties. Also, if you have a grill, cooking on one is better for draining off excess grease. I cook on low & go slow for just a couple of minutes since overcooking meat is disrespectful to the burger AND the cow!!

OMG, this is the best burger I have ever cooked! I did cut fat a bit by using 97% lean beef, and had 2 pounds to use, so upped the ingredients accordingly then followed the recipe. Got 6 huge burgers out of this. I do have to say that a little warning on the "taste explosion" factor that coated my chin, fingers, shirt, etc. would have been nice, but didn't decrease the flavor. ;-) Served with Kumato tomato, lettuce, avocado, and assorted other toppings. Thanks so much for sharing. Would have never found this one on my own-- did a search for most popular burger and this was one of them. On a side note, I did put the patties down on parchment and rolled them very thin with a rolling pin, then put the cheese in the middle, rolled up the edges and pressed it back to a uniform thickness so these would cook all the way through.

Garlic powder, salt and pepper and a pinch of sugar to season. Sharp Cheddar and Munster cheese makes a better flavor(my familys favorite). But choose the cheese that suits your tastes buds then you will have a great burger! I also dont pile it in the center, I normally shred or grate my own cheese fresh and mix it into the meat before making them into pattys. That way there is cheese through and through. Then of course a slice of sharp cheddar on top!
My son requested it and I made it. Of course we added garlic sautéed mushrooms and caramelized onions with bacon! Oh my gosh! So delicious!

Would have rated higher but American cheese?? Come on!
Any other sharp cheese would be good. Been making these for several years now and 1/4 to 3/8 " thick meat for each side. When grilling, when the cheese starts to evacuate the burger, the burger is done!

My late mother made these 60+ years ago. They were her special burgers served only when she and dad had the money to buy the extra pound or two of beef (yeah, times were tough back then, too). She called these delicious burgers "Stuffed Hamburger Patties", and used the only kind of cheese known back then -- cheddar. She would serve these with a brown gravy, some type of cooked vegetable, and usually a salad. Absolutely delicious! Oh, and by the way, we were in Louisiana {smiles}.

fabulous..... I delivered beer to Matt's Bar on 36th and Chicago in south Minneapolis in the late 1970's, where this burger originated. Did volunteer childcare work just blocks away at St. Joseph's Home for Children (Catholic). Literally have over a hundred of them.... this is the original recipe.
I converted it to the metric system

Kinda disappointing. Burgers shrunk up to hockey puck size. Cheese stayed put but...hmmm something not quite right. Just Ok. Not the best juicy burger I have ever made and other than piercing the burgers to let the steam out I won't use this recipe again
Not it. The cook actually knows the secret. This isn’t it.
I have made these for years, everybody loves them. I use different cheeses, be creative.

I grilled instead of using skillet, was good, I could taste all the ingredients. But still seemed like something was missing. It was just another burger to me, nothing extraordinary. I might try again and make some changes.
Yum! My patties shrunk quite a bit, but other than that these were great.
Fantastic burger! Juicy and cheesy goodness. Followed instructions to the T and it came out perfect.
